title.en: Exam Mastery — Mean, Median & Mode Together

headline.hi: Board Exam Ka Sabse Common Question Type!
headline.en: The Most Common Board Exam Question Type!

subtext.hi: Mean, Median aur Mode teeno ek hi data se — CBSE boards mein ye combo bahut common hai.
subtext.en: Mean, Median and Mode all from the same data — this combo is very common in CBSE boards.

text.hi: Statistics aur Probability milkar board exam mein 11 marks ke hote hain, aur inmein bhi sabse common question wo hota hai jisme ek hi data table se Mean, Median aur Mode teeno nikaalne ko kaha jaata hai (4 marks tak ka!). Ye lesson tumhe exact isi pattern ke liye taiyar karega.
text.en: Statistics and Probability together carry 11 marks in the board exam, and the single most common question type asks you to find Mean, Median AND Mode from the same data table (worth up to 4 marks!). This lesson prepares you exactly for that pattern.

content.hi: Exam tip: jab ek hi data se Mean, Median, Mode teeno poocha jaaye, toh ek hi baar mein poori table banao — Class, fᵢ, xᵢ, cf — sabhi columns ek saath, phir teeno formulas alag-alag apply karo. Isse time bachta hai aur mistakes kam hoti hain.
content.en: Exam tip: when Mean, Median and Mode are all asked from the same data, build ONE complete table — Class, fᵢ, xᵢ, cf — all columns together, then apply the three formulas separately. This saves time and reduces mistakes.

content.hi: Interesting fact: Mean, Median aur Mode teeno hamesha same nahi hote (sirf perfectly symmetric data mein same hote hain) — real data mein teeno thode alag-alag aate hain, aur unka comparison karna bhi board mein poocha jaata hai (jaise 'mode aur mean compare karo').
content.en: Interesting fact: Mean, Median and Mode aren't always equal (they match only for perfectly symmetric data) — in real data they usually differ slightly, and comparing them is sometimes asked in boards too (like 'compare the mode and mean').

content.hi: Empirical relationship (extra fact, useful for quick sanity-check): Mode ≈ 3×Median − 2×Mean. Isse tum apna answer verify bhi kar sakte ho.
content.en: Empirical relationship (extra fact, useful for a quick sanity check): Mode ≈ 3×Median − 2×Mean. You can use this to verify your answers too.

caption.hi: Ek table, teen formulas — Mean, Median, Mode teeno usi ek table se nikalte hain.
caption.en: One table, three formulas — Mean, Median and Mode are all found from that same one table.

problem.hi:
68 consumers ki monthly electricity consumption (units) di gayi hai. Median, Mean aur Mode teeno nikaalo.
Class: 65-85, 85-105, 105-125, 125-145, 145-165, 165-185, 185-205
Consumers: 4, 5, 13, 20, 14, 8, 4
problem.en:
The monthly electricity consumption (units) of 68 consumers is given. Find the Median, Mean and Mode.
Class: 65-85, 85-105, 105-125, 125-145, 145-165, 165-185, 185-205
Consumers: 4, 5, 13, 20, 14, 8, 4

steps.hi: MEDIAN: N=68, N/2=34. cf=42 (class 125-145) mein 34 pehli baar cross hoti hai → Median class=125-145. l=125,h=20,f=20,cf=22 → Median=125+[(34−22)/20]×20=125+12=137
steps.en: MEDIAN: N=68, N/2=34. cf=42 (class 125-145) is where 34 is first crossed → Median class=125-145. l=125,h=20,f=20,cf=22 → Median=125+[(34−22)/20]×20=125+12=137

steps.hi: Answer: Mean=137.06, Median=137, Mode=135.77 — teeno kaafi close hain!
steps.en: Answer: Mean=137.06, Median=137, Mode=135.77 — all three are quite close to each other!

problem.hi:
50 workers ki daily income (₹) di gayi hai. Mean, Median aur Mode teeno nikaalo.
Income: 100-120, 120-140, 140-160, 160-180, 180-200
Workers: 12, 14, 8, 6, 10
problem.en:
The daily income (₹) of 50 workers is given. Find the Mean, Median and Mode.
Income: 100-120, 120-140, 140-160, 160-180, 180-200
Workers: 12, 14, 8, 6, 10

steps.hi: Answer: Mean=145.2, Median=138.57, Mode=125 — is baar teeno mein zyada farak hai kyunki data thoda skewed hai
steps.en: Answer: Mean=145.2, Median=138.57, Mode=125 — this time there's more spread between them since the data is somewhat skewed

explanation.en: False — these three are equal only for perfectly symmetric data; in real data they usually differ.
